lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: a great business, but this lens's own price test fails and the price is 81% above the fair value of ₹172.

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: For every ₹100 it owes within a year, it holds ₹130 of cash, stock and dues coming in.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹8 cr vs working capital ₹801 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years
ch.r: Positive earnings in each of the last 10 years
ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: 22 dividends in 10 years with no gap longer than 18 months.

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +61%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹31 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.
You pay ₹5.58 for every ₹1 of net worth.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)
ch.w: With EPS ₹16.0 and book value ₹56 per share, Graham's ceiling price is ₹142.

lenses.st: Growth at a reasonable price · type: Fast grower
lenses.sp: First sorts the company by type (this one looks like a fast grower), then wants growth at a sensible PEG with low debt.
lenses.vd: In Peter Lynch's spirit: a great business, but the price is 81% above the fair value of ₹172.

ch.r: PEG < 1 attractive, ~1 fair, ≥ 2 expensive
ch.w: PE 19.6 divided by EPS growth 25.9% a year (growth measured over 3 yrs).

ch.r: Debt-to-equity below 0.35
ch.w: ₹0 borrowed for every ₹100 of shareholders' money.

ch.r: EPS growth 20–25% a year

rs.t: Price ₹312 is 81% above the consensus fair value of ₹172 (🛡️ Strict view, used for this verdict) (0 of 3 methods say cheap, 3 say expensive)

🟡 Profit jumped 1.8× – valued on normal years (profit jumped 2.0× while sales grew 1.2× (₹897 cr vs a normal ₹445 cr)); new level confirmed: 2 quarters reported since the spike year (FY ending 2026-03-31); 2 reached the new level (₹138 cr a quarter = 80% of ₹692 cr ÷ 4)
Has very little debt – better than 92% of Construction & EPC
Customers pay in about 45 days – better than 92% of Construction & EPC
Earns 28% a year on all the money it uses – better than 83% of Construction & EPC

v4.ll: Passes Fisher, Greenblatt, F-score-style checks; great business but price not right for Graham, Buffett, Munger, Lynch, Agrawal; fails Kedia-style checks
ch: Drops to Hold if the quality score falls below 70 (now 74); to Avoid below 50.

Buy zone: below ₹129 (25% under the consensus fair value ₹172, 🛡️ Strict view), if the view's own conditions hold, confidence is Medium or High and the trend is up. Accumulate zone: ₹147–₹198 (consensus ₹172).
Moves to Trim above ₹224 (30% over fair value).

Any new serious red flag (auditor resigns mid-term, pledge above 25%, SEBI order, negative net worth, weak cash conversion together with high accruals, distress with interest cover below 1.5×) moves it straight to Avoid.
